thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Increased 5xx error rate detected for hosted API in ap-southeast-1 — 12m sustained. Pager sent to infra oncall.
alex: seeing 502/503s from customer telemetry, started ~06:12 UTC. spikes to ~18% error-rate per host group.
maya: confirmed on Grafana — latency up and 5xx spikes. Most affected pop is ap-southeast-1, subset of edge nodes.
alex: paging Raj (neteng) — can you check GeoDNS and external resolver behavior?
raj: on it. quick check — doing dig against our edge IPs via Cloudflare and Route53 geo queries.
raj: running: `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.prod` and `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.prod` — results inconsistent across resolvers. some returning old IP set, some returning SERVFAIL intermittently.
sarah: noticed spike in resolver timeouts from our probe fleet, correlates with the timing.
jules: incident-bot created INC-2026-043, severity: high (customer-impacting).
oncall-bot: On-call handoff: @maya is primary until 06:45 UTC, paging infra oncall.
leo: quick note — no recent infra deploys in the last 3 hours. not a release regression.
raj: cloudflare status API shows a partial edge disruption in APAC (status page: https://cloudflarestatus.example/incident/xyz). routing / resolver caching could be returning inconsistent answers.
maya: can someone run `dig +trace` from ap-southeast vantage? need evidence of propagation skew.
alex: pasted dig outputs from a probe:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.prod
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1
;; AUTHORITY SECTION: ns-2.route53.example.com. 300 IN SOA ...
```
and
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.prod
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 67890
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.prod. 60 IN A 34.198.120.5
api.redwood.prod. 60 IN A 35.190.44.7
```
raj: that matches — Cloudflare resolvers returning SERVFAIL for certain ECMP paths. Route53 answers are fine. likely an external resolver/regional flap between CF and our origin or authoritative chain.
netops-bot: Notifying Cloudflare support channel with dig traces and timestamps.
maya: mitigation options — (1) Change GeoDNS policy to prefer us-east as failover for APAC temporarily (2) Reduce GeoDNS TTLs (can't change quickly? TTL is 60s currently) (3) Add a temporary static edge IP in ap-southeast mapped via alternate provider. Thoughts?
raj: we can adjust GeoDNS weights via control plane now. doing a controlled shift of 30% traffic away from affected APAC edge nodes to us-east-1 (failover) for next 20m.
alex: do it but be careful — clients from APAC hitting us-east will see higher latency. need to notify support and throttle rate-limited routes.
sarah: raising retries/backoff on ingress could mask failures for clients; ops will update client retry policy for the regional proxy for the next 30m.
jules: I've drafted a customer advisory note for impacted tenants, adding that degraded latency but reduced errors expected. publishing to status.redwood.io in 10m.
raj: UPDATE: Applied GeoDNS weight change at 06:22 UTC — shifted 35% traffic to us-east-1 and 10% to eu-west as backup.
maya: monitoring... error-rate dropped from 18% -> 6% over 5m. good signal.
leo: netflow shows fewer SYN resets in ap-southeast after the shift.
alex: Cloudflare support responded — they confirm an APAC resolver cluster had an internal failure, returning SERVFAIL for some EDNS0 queries between 06:03-06:26 UTC. they're triggering mitigation.
netops-bot: Cloudflare ticket CF-2026-998 updated: root cause identified, global fix rolling. estimated full resolution 07:10 UTC.
raj: plan to gradually rollback GeoDNS weights to normal after 07:20 UTC once CF confirms stable answers.
sarah: are there any customer-specific failures? metrics show three high-volume customers with elevated errors in APAC — CS notified and case opened.
jules: support updates queued. sending targeted DM to account owners.
maya: creating post-incident checklist: capture probe dig logs, route53 cache TTLs, GeoDNS weight history, and timeline of Cloudflare fix.
alex: also capture sample client traces showing 5xx -> successful after failover for regression analysis.
raj: running `aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ` to confirm no conflicting records. all authoritative records unchanged.
maya: next steps: keep incident open until 07:30 UTC, monitor for reappearance, rollback weights after CF stable message, publish postmortem draft.
oncall-bot: Handed off to morning oncall @sarah at 06:45 UTC.
raj: rolling rollback scheduled at 07:25 UTC — will move back increments of 10% every 3 minutes if error-rate remains <2%.
alex: thanks team. great quick coordination. :heart:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: condition resolved at 07:34 UTC after full rollback and CF confirmation. root cause: Cloudflare APAC resolver cluster transient failure causing intermittent SERVFAILs and resolver inconsistency. action items assigned in tracking board.
